caption: The drawing features an ornate metal window grill composed of vertical and horizontal bars with decorative scrollwork. The grill is primarily brown, suggesting it is made of iron or similar metal. The vertical bars are evenly spaced and intersected by three horizontal bars, creating a rectangular grid. At each intersection, as well as at intervals along the bars, are symmetrical floral or scroll-like decorations. The top and bottom edges of the grill curve outward, with the top also featuring a more elaborate central decorative fleur-de-lis element. The overall composition is centered on a plain off-white background, with no other objects present. There is a small inscription with a name, "W.K. Kecombiel," near the bottom right of the drawing.
title: Iron Grille at Window
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
